Implementation Plan Implementation plan for issue #6339: the clarify-respond worker's answer must decide every question before it is posted Planning ref: `claude/eloquent-gauss-nhi442` @ `e9eaf61e5a824a86dd26c39d2a0b227c00644074`. This matches the integration branch metadata, so there is no mismatch. Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends scripts/auto_decisions.py Scope-mode justification: The finding names one gap. In `.github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml`, "Parse and post answer" (around line 1167) runs `scripts/orchestrate_parse_and_post_answer.sh`, and that script only rejects an empty `CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE`. So an answer that leaves questions out or picks an option that doesn't exist is posted as a bot `/answer`, and planning starts. The answers chose to check both modes on the shared path (Q1=A) and to fill gaps with RECOMMENDED options, failing closed when a gap has no RECOMMENDED option (Q2=A). `scripts/auto_decisions.py` already parses the questions (`_question_blocks`), the worker's picks (`_answer_sections`) and the RECOMMENDED markers (`parse_questions`). The existing "Standalone RECOMMENDED fallback" step already shows how to fail closed and page CRITICAL. One new subcommand plus one workflow step covers the whole requirement. No new script, dependency or external interface is needed, so Boil the Lake points to the complete version: both modes, filling, attribution and tests, all in this PR. Automation (§20) - No new script. This extends the existing `scripts/auto_decisions.py` (new `complete` subcommand) and adds one step to the existing `.github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml`. - Entry point: no new one. The step runs inside the existing `respond` job, which the `issue_comment: created` trigger on the clarify questions comment already starts (through `internal-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml` here, and `ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml` in consumer repos). - No long-running supervisor, no database work, and no entry needed in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`. - `auto_decisions.py` is already in the workflow's staged-support list (line 333). It is staged for both modes, from the same ref as the workflow. 1. Files likely to change - `scripts/auto_decisions.py`: new `complete` subcommand and a `complete_answers()` function. `render()` / `_format_entry()` accept an optional `source` on each decision. - `.github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml`: - new step "Answer completeness guard" (`id: answer_completeness`), placed right before "Data-provision guard"; - `&& steps.answer_completeness.outputs.complete != 'false'` added to the `if:` of "Data-provision guard" and "Parse and post answer"; - "Record standalone auto-decisions" credits filled-in picks to "RECOMMENDED fallback". - `tests/test_clarify_respond_standalone.py`: unit tests for `complete_answers()`, step-level tests using the existing `_steps` / `_substitute` / `_stub_gh` / `_env` / `_install_scripts` helpers, and wiring contract tests. - `agents.md`: one sentence in the "Standalone issues answered by the clarify-respond worker" bullet, and the new log prefix `CLARIFY_RESPOND_ANSWER_COMPLETENESS` added to the stable-prefix list (bullet list and `LOG_PREFIX.name=` lines). - `changelog.d/6339-clarify-respond-answer-completeness.md`: new fragment. - Not changed: - `scripts/orchestrate_parse_and_post_answer.sh`. `clarify.yml` (line 1379) also calls it, but only with RECOMMENDED answers built by `auto_decisions.py parse`, which are complete by construction. Adding a questions-file requirement to the poster would break that caller. - `clarify.yml`. - `scripts/clarify_data_provision_guard.py`. 2. Functions and modules to implement `auto_decisions.complete_answers(questions_text, answers_text) -> dict` - Parse the questions with `_question_blocks`. If no `Q` is found, return `status="unparseable"`; the answer can't be checked, so it fails closed. - Collect every pick per Q-ID, using the same section rules as `_answer_sections`: the pre-heading region and the `DECISIONS` section. Keep all picks, not just the first. Also match a looser line shape `^\s*\*{0,2}Q\d+\*{0,2}\s*:` in those sections, so lowercase or garbled decision lines count as invalid instead of being ignored. - A pick is permitted when it is one of: - (a) a letter combination `[A-Z](\+[A-Z])*` with no repeated letter, where every letter is one of that question's parsed option letters; - (b) one of `DERIVE_FROM_REPO`, `SYNTHESIZE`, `REFRAME`, `ESCALATE`, the worker's contracted vocabulary at `prompts/mode-clarify-respond.txt:132` (see D2). - Classify each question: - `missing`: no pick; - `invalid`: a pick that isn't permitted, or more than one distinct pick (`conflicting`). - Q-IDs that are answered but don't appear in the questions go in `extra`. - If nothing is missing, invalid or extra: return `status="complete"` and `answers` byte-identical to the input. - Otherwise, for each missing or invalid question, take the RECOMMENDED pick (same logic as `parse_questions`). If any of those questions has no RECOMMENDED option, return `status="blocked"`. Also return `blocked` when the answer has an `ESCALATION` section but a gap is still missing or invalid (see D4). - Otherwise return `status="filled"` with a rewritten `answers`: - a canonical `DECISIONS:` block, one `Q: ` line per parsed question in order. Valid worker picks are kept verbatim and gaps get the RECOMMENDED pick; - then a `RATIONALE:` block with one line per filled Q-ID: `Q: RECOMMENDED option used; the worker answer gave no permitted decision (missing|invalid: ).`; - then the worker's original text with its `DECISIONS` heading and every decision-like line in the pre-heading and `DECISIONS` regions removed, and its `RATIONALE` entries (including continuation lines) for filled Q-IDs removed. - Return shape: `{"status", "answers", "filled": [...], "missing": [...], "invalid": [{"qid","pick","reason"}], "extra": [...], "undecided": [...]}`. Every echoed pick goes through `_clean` and is cut to 40 characters. CLI: `complete --questions-file

--answers-file

` - JSON on stdout. Exit codes follow the existing convention: 0 for ok (any status), 1 for bad input, 2 for an unreadable file. - Update the module docstring. `_format_entry` / `render` - When a decision dict carries a non-empty string `source`, use `_clean(decision["source"])` instead of the global `--source`. - A `source` that isn't a string raises `UsageError`. - No existing decision key is called `source`, so there is no collision. Workflow step "Answer completeness guard" (`id: answer_completeness`) - `if:` is identical to "Data-provision guard" (`respond == 'true' && (run_codex success || cache_hit || standalone_fallback.ready)`), so it covers orchestrator mode, standalone mode, semantic-cache hits and the fallback output. - Env: `TG_BOT_SECRET`, `TG_CHAT_ID`, `GH_TOKEN`, `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`, `CLARIFY_RESPOND_MODE: ${{ steps.check_orchestrator.outputs.mode }}`, all mirroring the fallback step. - Body: - If the script, the clarification file or the answer file is missing, log `::error::` and `exit 1`, the same way the data guard does. - Run `python3 scripts/auto_decisions.py complete …` into `${RUNTIME_DIR}/answer_completeness.json`. A non-zero exit means `exit 1`. - `complete`: write `complete=true`. - `filled`: write `.answers` to `CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE`, raise a `::warning::` with the diff, and write `complete=true` plus `filled=`. - `blocked` or `unparseable`: write `complete=false`, log `STANDALONE_AUTO_DECIDE issue=… outcome=skip reason=incomplete_answer_undecided …` in standalone mode, and page CRITICAL with `tg_send_phase_tracked "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" "clarify" … "CRITICAL"`. Then exit 0, as the fallback step does. - Every path logs `CLARIFY_RESPOND_ANSWER_COMPLETENESS issue= mode= outcome=complete|filled|blocked|unparseable missing= invalid= extra= filled=`. "Record standalone auto-decisions" - New env `CLARIFY_RESPOND_FILLED_QIDS: ${{ steps.answer_completeness.outputs.filled || '' }}`, validated against `^Q[1-9][0-9]*(,Q[1-9][0-9]*)*$`; anything else is treated as empty. - After `from-answers`, `jq` sets `.source = "clarify comment ${CLARIFICATION_COMMENT_ID}, RECOMMENDED fallback"` on decisions whose `qid` is in that list. - Add `filled=` to the existing `STANDALONE_AUTO_DECIDE … outcome=answered` line. This is an additive field. 3. Data structures affected - New runtime artefact `${RUNTIME_DIR}/answer_completeness.json`. - New step outputs `complete` and `filled`. - Decision dicts get an optional `source` key, which `render` reads. - No change to GitHub labels, the processed-command ledger, the memory schemas or the auto-decisions comment marker or format. 4. API and interface changes - New CLI subcommand `auto_decisions.py complete`. Existing subcommands behave the same. - New stable log prefix `CLARIFY_RESPOND_ANSWER_COMPLETENESS`. - The posted `/answer` body is unchanged when the answer is complete. A filled answer gets a canonical `DECISIONS:` block first, which the planner and `from-answers` already parse. Data flow: 1. The worker, cache hit or fallback writes `CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE`. 2. New: Answer completeness guard, with three outcomes: - complete: no change; - filled: `CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE` is rewritten and `filled=Q…` is set; - blocked or unparseable: `complete=false` and a CRITICAL page. The next two steps are skipped, and the record step is skipped because `SKIP_AUTO_ANSWER` stays unset. 3. Data-provision guard. It now also checks the filled-in RECOMMENDED picks. 4. Parse and post answer: loop guard, ESCALATE handling, then `/answer`. 5. Record standalone auto-decisions, with filled Q-IDs credited to "RECOMMENDED fallback".
